summary: Unexpected variant tilt to low-memory replica causing prolonged KV warmup and 504s
description:
Issue summary: During the 2026-03-10 09:15 UTC traffic spike for HyperRetail's dedicated pool, a routing decision caused a subset of requests to be routed to a low-memory variant (sparse-mem-replica) that was not sufficiently warmed. Impact: ~10-15% of requests for the customer returned 504/timeouts or experienced multi-second token wait times for ~20 minutes. This affected storefront search latency and caused customer alerts.

Impact: Customer-reported elevated error rate and slow inference for critical search endpoints during peak traffic. No customer data leakage observed.

Environment: Dedicated pool for HyperRetail in prod-us-east. Autoscaling events were in-flight; new replicas launching. The routing policy includes a capacity-aware fallback that prefers low-cost variants under contention.

Expected behavior: Under capacity pressure the platform should route to warmed fallback variants or gracefully queue with backpressure, not shift a significant fraction of live traffic to replicas that require prolonged KV cache warmup.

Observed behavior: A traffic shift (tilt) routed ~12% of requests to a low-memory replica type which had cold or partially-cold KV caches, causing long per-request warmup stalls and 504s.

Steps already taken: throttled customer burst, temporarily disabled the low-memory fallback for the HyperRetail pool, coordinated with SRE to increase target warm replicas.
steps_to_reproduce: Provision a dedicated pool with mixed-capacity variants (high-memory and low-memory replicas)
Simulate a sudden traffic surge that triggers autoscaler and fallback routing (5000 req/min for 5 minutes)
Observe routing decisions in router logs: look for >10% traffic to sparse-mem replicas that recently transitioned from initializing
Inspect serving-runtime traces for KV cache misses and long warmup durations
observed_behavior: Requests were diverted to sparse-mem replicas that returned intermittent 504s and showed long wait times due to synchronous KV warmup operations. Latency plots show a step increase in tail latency aligned with the autoscaler add events.
expected_behavior: Platform should maintain traffic on warmed replicas, or use a staged ramp/fan-out to new replicas that pre-warm KV caches without taking live traffic until warm. Fallbacks should prefer replicas with warm KV cache or use queued warmup prior to routing production traffic.
investigation_notes: Router decision logs indicate the capacity-aware fallback policy weights low-cost variants when available_capacity < threshold
Sparse-mem replicas were marked 'ready' by the scheduler once container started but before KV prefetch completed
Serving-runtime traces show synchronous KV prefetch running on first requests, blocking token generation for ~1.2-2.5s per affected request
Autoscaler events: 3 new sparse-mem replicas spun up between 09:12-09:18 UTC; router immediately included them in candidate pool
Hypothesis: readiness gating currently checks container liveness only; KV cache readiness is not gated leading to early routing
Related runbook: routing/fallback-policy.md suggests a warmup probe feature but it was not enabled for this customer's deployment

comments: 2026-03-10 09:40 UTC - Customer (HyperRetail Ops): We're seeing ~10% error rate and search queries are timing out during the morning spike. This started around 09:12 UTC. Can you confirm if you pulled a different model or variant?
2026-03-10 09:48 UTC - Marta Diaz (Support): Acknowledged. We've opened an incident and are investigating. Can you share a sample request id that failed?
2026-03-10 09:52 UTC - HyperRetail Ops: sample ids: def456, ghi789. We noticed increased 504s; traffic pattern aligned with internal campaign.

2026-03-10 10:05 UTC - Evan Kim (SRE): Initial router logs show candidate inclusion of sparse-mem replicas during autoscale. I'm temporarily disabling sparse-mem fallback for the hyperretail pool and increasing warm replica targets. Monitoring for error rate to drop.
2026-03-10 10:23 UTC - Marta Diaz (Support): After disabling fallback, error rate decreased to baseline but tail latency still elevated for a short window. Customer confirms storefront is recovering.

2026-03-11 14:10 UTC - Rahul Patel (Runtime Eng): Investigated KV prefetch readiness gating. Found readiness probe only checks container/GRPC health; will propose change to include kv_prefetch complete flag before marking replica as ready. Drafting PR.

2026-03-12 09:30 UTC - Evan Kim (SRE): Mitigation steps applied: (1) disabled low-memory fallback for dedicated pools by default for one hour after scale events, (2) added router metric to alert when >5% traffic is routed to replicas with kv_prefetch_status!=complete. Opening follow-up task for permanent fix.
resolution: Mitigated: disabled low-memory fallback for HyperRetail's pool and increased warm replica target; error rates returned to normal. Long-term fix: add KV-prefetch readiness gating and update fallback policy to prefer warmed replicas or stagger traffic to new replicas until kv cache is ready.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation removed the immediate customer impact within ~12 minutes
Engineering action item: platform PR to extend readiness probe to include kv_prefetch_status (assigned to Runtime Eng)
Policy action item: change default fallback policy for dedicated pools to avoid low-memory variants until explicit opt-in
Follow-up ticket created for implementation and rollout: INT-3399
